title: FROM MILK TO MEAT: TRAIN ALL YOUR SENSES

sense.text:
This is for the women, and the brothers have to implement it too. When a sister has a baby, the afterbirth carries the nutrients out with it, and God gives her time to replenish herself: forty days for a male child, eighty days for a girl. In that time she needs help.

“And Mary abode with her about three months, and returned to her own house.” Those were the last three months of Elisabeth’s pregnancy. Mary stayed with her to help her out and assist her.

“Now Elisabeth’s full time came that she should be delivered; and she brought forth a son. And her neighbours and her cousins heard how the Lord had shewed great mercy upon her; and they rejoiced with her.”

Her neighbours and her cousins came to help her: with food, with washing, with the clothes and the laundry, all of it. That is what the sisters must do for one another.

A lot of times sisters have their babies on their own. They take care of the baby alone, and they get depressed, confused and struggling, and then they argue with the husband when he comes home from work, because they need help. We have to get back to what the scriptures say: the women, the neighbours and the cousins, helped her.

“And it came to pass, that on the eighth day they came to circumcise the child; and they called him Zacharias, after the name of his father.” It only takes one person to circumcise a child, but the point is that the neighbours and cousins came and were there with her.

The class is from milk to meat: train all your senses. Brothers ask how leadership knows what it knows, how it can foresee certain things happening. It comes from doing this for many years; a lot of it is patterns that are seen. The men especially have to train their senses, because the men are going to be judging matters, and the first thing to do is exercise those senses: learn, apply, and the Holy Spirit will take over, and you will catch things other people miss.

“Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine? them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts.” How do we know, how do we discern, how do we get understanding? The knowledge is the law, sought at the priest’s mouth, and the doctrine is the commandments. The Lord teaches them that have come off the milk.

“For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little.” That is how we explain the Bible: by the scriptures. The answer to a question might be found someplace else in the book.

People ask how we do that. We are the messengers of God, and that is why we are able to flow through this Bible. It is not man’s doing; it is the application of God’s laws. Once you get experience in teaching and applying, you will see how the spirit works on you.

Street teachers know it. A question is posed in the street and you recite a scripture you don’t normally go to; the recall kicks in when you are challenged, and that is the Lord working with your memory. But a brother who gets stuck in the middle of teaching, when the people out there don’t even know the scriptures, has something not right in him. The spirit of God is not with him.

“To whom he said, This is the rest wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest; and this is the refreshing: yet they would not hear.” Some people refuse to hear the word of God. This is the rest the Lord will cause us to rest in, the peace that comes with serving him.

precepts.why:
“For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth.” The law is the knowledge we are supposed to be seeking at the priest’s mouth. That is the knowledge Isaiah asks about: whom shall he teach knowledge?

“For he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.” The priest is the messenger of the Lord, so what he is teaching, explaining and expounding on is sent from the Most High God and our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.

What is the doctrine? “For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.” The Lord says he gives us good doctrine, and with it, do not forsake the law of the Most High. The doctrine Isaiah speaks of is bound up with the law.

“The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life.” The doctrine is the knowledge of the commandments.

“And they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.” Those that do the things that please the Most High are the keepers of the commandments, and they receive the fruit of the tree of immortality. That is what we are all doing this for: we are all doing it because we want eternal life.

sense.text: “Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings.” You have to remove all of those things out of your spirit first.

“As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby.” If you want to go from milk to meat, you first have to desire the sincere milk of the word, and grow thereby like a baby.

If you are not in the scriptures every day, your mind is not right and you are not really in this truth. This is all we have. Four chapters a day: you would have to miss them on purpose. Some are not strong readers, and that is understood, but put on the Bible app or a reading on YouTube and read along; four chapters take about five minutes that way.

Missing them is consciously saying, not with your words but with your actions, I do not desire the sincere milk of the word. And then you wonder why you don’t grow. The way we know the things we know is that we have been rehearsing this over and over again. When something is spoken that seems deep, it is because we have seen it or experienced it already, and we are trying to show you how to handle it.

“If so be ye have tasted that the Lord is gracious.” How is the Lord gracious toward us? He did not kill us for the sins we committed; he allowed us to learn this knowledge so that we can repent. That is the Lord imparting mercy upon us, giving us a chance to get right.

precepts.why:
The Jews at Jerusalem write to their brethren in Egypt: “God be gracious unto you, and remember his covenant that he made with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, his faithful servants; And give you all an heart to serve him.” The Lord has been gracious unto us because he gave us a heart and understanding to serve him.

We understand what the will of God is. People spend a whole lifetime in church and don’t know that Christ is black; how you don’t know that in 2026 can’t be understood. That you have to keep the commandments, that you can’t eat pork, that a woman can’t wear pants: those are very basic things, but God was gracious to us that we know his will.

“And to do his will, with a good courage and a willing mind.” That is the sincere desire: a willing mind. You have to want to do this. Brothers wonder why they are not growing, and it is because it is not important to them; it is not the apple of their eye. So when it is time to sit down and go through prophecies, it is way over their heads, because they can’t even do something basic like reading four chapters a day.

The ones that are serious, with a willing mind, are on the streets putting their labour in, though most of us do this part time and all have jobs. A brother misses a meeting because his car gave problems: he could have taken his wife’s car, or got on a Zoom call. His spirit is not there, and then he wonders why he is a decade in and still a soldier. Had it been a million dollars, he would have walked there. When the bishops came in there were no online classes; you had to get on a train to the school, be at Sabbath service, the trooper program, seven hours of camp 101 on a Sunday and a class during the week, just to hold post at camp. Now there are classes twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week, and brothers still don’t know who the tribe in the valley is.

“And open your hearts in his law and commandments, and send you peace.” Those come in conjunction. If you want peace in your life, in this truth, in your marriage and your friendships, you have to have a willing mind to come and serve God. That is the rest Isaiah spoke of. The Lord is gracious to show us who we are and what his will is, and it has to be important to you.

“And hear your prayers, and be at one with you, and never forsake you in time of trouble.” Then God hears your prayers and is at one with you, and he will never forsake you in the time of trouble.

sense.text: “Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.” If you believe you just pray, God give me understanding so I can break down Revelation, and it comes, that is not how it works. You pray to God, and God will tell you to study to show thyself approved, rightly dividing the word. You have to choose this.

“I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.” Sometimes your job, or whatever you have, becomes more important, and then you wonder why you can’t grow. Our chief love is the word of God. Jobs and careers are just to get by in this captivity; they should not be the focal point of your life. Seek the kingdom first, and everything else shall be added.

“Neither compared I unto her any precious stone, because all gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay before her.” All gold is as a little sand next to wisdom.

Why is wisdom better than gold or silver? Those things are corruptible and won’t last into the kingdom to come; they can be stolen or destroyed. And what do people do with gold? They sell it. If you had gold right now you could sell some and make some money, but in time it runs out. Wisdom never runs out, because with wisdom you get the understanding to make more.

“I loved her above health and beauty, and chose to have her instead of light: for the light that cometh from her never goeth out.” The light that comes from the word is a light that will never go out. Choose wisdom above all things; prefer the Lord above all things. If you want understanding, call upon God and he will give it to you, but we have to make him first.
“I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.”

“For she is a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of God.” This is a treasure that never fails, and those that use it, that apply it in their lives, become friends of God, “being commended for the gifts that come from learning.”

Some of those gifts are the senses this class is about, a certain level of understanding. Those who have been studying for a while have run across a scripture they never heard before and known at once that it lines up perfectly with what they already studied, without calling anybody for confirmation. That doesn’t mean you don’t get counsel. It means that when the Holy Spirit takes over you, God guides you and makes it clear, because all the precepts line up. It is euphoric; it is almost the greatest feeling you can get.

“God hath granted me to speak as I would, and to conceive as is meet for the things that are given me: because it is he that leadeth unto wisdom, and directeth the wise.” It is God that leads unto wisdom and directs the wise.

“For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.” Wisdom is a pure influence from God. When you are tapped into it, it influences you in the right direction: don’t do that, be cautious, be careful, go over here and teach, don’t worry about this job. The spirit of God moves you and tells you something, like a whisper in your ear, something speaking in your spirit.

But you have to be right with God. If you are not right with God and you are watching porn, that is not God speaking; that is Satan speaking to you, your own lust moving you in the wrong direction.

To wrap the thought up: we pray for understanding and it is given to us. God grants it to us if we love him, and it leads and directs our ways.

“For in his hand are both we and our words; all wisdom also, and knowledge of workmanship. For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements.”

God gave Solomon to understand because he loved wisdom: he let him know the creation, how things were made. The churches and many groups cannot explain Genesis 1; they don’t understand the firmament. Genesis 1 is hard reading to them. He showed Solomon because he preferred wisdom above all riches.

“The beginning, ending, and midst of the times”: God gave Solomon to understand the midst of times and the last days. He gave that to David, to Ezra, to many of the prophets, and in this time he has given it to us. The deacons and bishops going through prophecies and explaining Revelation like it has never been heard: that is the pure influence of God working on that person. It is not subject to one person; it could be put on any one of us who prefers wisdom above sceptres, thrones and gold and makes it our chief love. That begins the transition from milk to meat.

The turning of the sun, the seasons, the stars, the natures of living creatures: all of that comes from preferring wisdom, preferring God above all. The one touched on in this class is “the reasonings of men”: how a man thinks, what a man’s nature is. Men that judge matters hear a situation and know there is more to it, even before they know what it is, because certain things line up when you look at a person’s spirit.

That is why it is good to talk to brothers face to face. If you are not right, your face says something different from what is coming out of your mouth, and a discerning spirit can read between the lines.

“And all such things as are either secret or manifest, them I know.” Things that are secret, not visible, the influence of God lets Solomon know. God influences his servants to understand secret things that people may not see, and makes them plain.

So when they ask in the street, how do you do that, where did you get that, how did you understand that: we are called of God, and it is his influence upon us. He directs our paths, but we must choose him. This is the exercising of your senses.

“That the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give unto you the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him.” The knowledge of God is a revelation: understanding things that must be revealed. People don’t understand the Bible because God has not imparted that revelation to them. We don’t read the Bible like a textbook. This is spiritual; it has to be shown to you, and you have to love him first for him to reveal it.
“The eyes of your understanding being enlightened; that ye may know what is the hope of his calling, and what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints.”

“And what is the exceeding greatness of his power to us-ward who believe, according to the working of his mighty power.” How great a power we have in God, that he has imparted it to us. In this world we are superheroes, larger than life. We may not get respect from these nations, but God sees what we are doing, turning things right side up on these streets.

We are the only ones making real noise. The church is on lunch break. The Nation of Islam is no more out in the streets. Other Israelite groups argue about multiple wives. We are the only ones out there pleading the cause of all people and bringing them to repentance, raising men from the grassroots: young men and children coming in off the street, where others only have the grandchildren of the people already there.

A young man in a video had the image of Christ as the wallpaper on his phone and listened to Original Royalty music; he called it God, and had never yet been in a school. He was learning by watching. That is a glimpse of the ripple effect, the next generation being reached, and the spirit of God directing the brothers to stand out there that day and run into him. We have not yet fully seen the power of God exposed; the Lord is going to manifest it soon enough.

“The wisdom of a learned man cometh by opportunity of leisure: and he that hath little business shall become wise.” Leisure is the time you have off work, your free time. What you do with it decides whether you become wise.

Read on into the next chapter and it shows what the man does with that leisure: he gives his mind to the law of the Most High. That is why 38:24 is precepted with 39:1.

“But he that giveth his mind to the law of the most High, and is occupied in the meditation thereof, will seek out the wisdom of all the ancient, and be occupied in prophecies.” The ancient are Isaiah, Jeremiah, John the Revelator.

In your leisure time, when you are off work, you are not brain rotting on YouTube shorts or porn. Porn is destroying the minds of the men, and of whoever is doing it. It is a sickness and a disease; you will be no good for the Lord or for anything else, and eventually you act out that behaviour, and some will end up in jail behind it, and we are not bailing you out, little nasty.

The way you seek out the wisdom of the ancient is to get around leadership. Fifty brothers stand at the podium and a brother stands in the back. Drop everything; you have the opportunity to learn, so learn. Nobody’s arm is being twisted. When class is over and there is a chance to get around leadership, take advantage of it, and do it with your local leadership too: whoever in your school has understanding, get close to him and learn.

“He will keep the sayings of the renowned men: and where subtil parables are, he will be there also. He will seek out the secrets of grave sentences, and be conversant in dark parables.” Seeking out dark sentences, being around the ancients.

“He shall serve among great men, and appear before princes: he will travel through strange countries; for he hath tried the good and the evil among men.” How is he able to try the good and evil? By reason of use, with his senses exercised.

Some people can’t discern between right and wrong, good and evil, because they refuse to make this the principal thing in their lives and refuse to come around leadership to learn. Some are just playing Israelite: they put on the purple and the fringes but are not really in the mix. That takes more energy than sitting down to learn. A brother like that can be talked into going to a strip club right after breaking bread, because his spiritual compass is so off kilter. Another, given a little favour with a job and a car, went to pick up a woman when he didn’t have a pot to piss in nor a window to throw it out of. His discernment is gone.

By studying four chapters a day, using our leisure, being occupied in meditation and prophecy and keeping the sayings of renowned men, we serve among great men and appear before princes. We have met vice presidents, secretaries of state, prime ministers, mayors, governors and police commissioners. We get emails to come on a show and argue with ten Christians; we don’t do that stupidity. We don’t have time for the foolishness of negroes. To change the minds of the masses of our people we can’t get distracted with kids’ games. We are not here to convince Esau that he is the devil; we are here to gain our people over to Christ, so we meet with the people who can make a major impact.
“He will give his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and will pray before the most High, and will open his mouth in prayer, and make supplication for his sins.” He is going to repent.

“When the great Lord will, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding.” When the Lord has seen that you have been making a conscious change, mortifying and disciplining yourself, then he begins to fill you with the spirit of understanding. First you get around great men to learn, repent and get your mind right; then the Lord can use you.

Before that, the strong meat is not for you. You have to learn the simple things: no whoremonger shall enter the kingdom, wear your fringes, remember the sabbath day to keep it holy, know the tribes. Years ago a brother taking the officer test, more than ten years ago and almost impossible to fail, could only fill in ten of the twelve tribes of Israel.

“He shall pour out wise sentences, and give thanks unto the Lord in his prayer.”

“He shall direct his counsel and knowledge, and in his secrets shall he meditate.” The secrets are in the scriptures, and the Lord is going to reveal them; he will meditate upon these things. This is the transition from milk to meat.

“He shall shew forth that which he hath learned, and shall glory in the law of the covenant of the Lord.” Out of his mouth he shows forth all the wisdom he has accumulated over years of studying, applying, getting around renowned men and learning the scriptures.

“Many shall commend his understanding; and so long as the world endureth, it shall not be blotted out; his memorial shall not depart away, and his name shall live from generation to generation.” That is what you want for your name: when you leave this earth, your name still rings bells and is still part of the conversation, for how God moved you, worked with you and used you as his disciple.

For that you have to level up. A teacher’s classes can’t keep talking about the same things, regurgitating the same class over and over. You have to grow in understanding and application to teach the people.

“If he die, he shall leave a greater name than a thousand: and if he live, he shall increase it.” If you live, your name keeps growing. That is a man ever evolving, always getting better, until we measure up to the full stature of Christ.

“Yet have I more to say, which I have thought upon; for I am filled as the moon at the full.” He has much more to express. “Hearken unto me, ye holy children, and bud forth as a rose growing by the brook of the field”: hearken unto me and learn.

precepts.why:
The New Testament says something very similar to having tried the good and the evil among men: “But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.”

The whole class is about training your senses to discern. He that has tried the good and the evil among men has had his senses exercised by reason of use: by giving his mind to the law, getting around renowned men and travelling. That is how he is able to try them.

Sirach says hearken unto me and learn, and at the end of his book he says what he has written: “Jesus the son of Sirach of Jerusalem hath written in this book the instruction of understanding and knowledge, who out of his heart poured forth wisdom.”

“Blessed is he that shall be exercised in these things; and he that layeth them up in his heart shall become wise.” If you lay this up, you will become wise.

“For if he do them, he shall be strong to all things.” If he applies these commandments he will be strong to all things, “for the light of the Lord leadeth him, who giveth wisdom to the godly.” The Lord will make you strong in the word. You will be able to confound, and you won’t get fooled with nonsense. Some brothers don’t know simple things in the Bible; one was almost convinced that Christ wasn’t black.

sense.text:
“The Lord created man of the earth, and turned him into it again. He gave them few days, and a short time, and power also over the things therein. He endued them with strength by themselves, and made them according to his image.”

God gave us, his creation, the sons of God, the ability to think on our own, to create, build, engineer, help and heal, on this earthly level, as a shadow of him.

And because he gave that to us, the nations fear us right now. God’s wisdom is on us. We don’t have military power. The power we have is this book, and it is the only power we need. This is what has the nations trembling, and the reason they don’t want to talk to us: we could use this book and confound the world. Our strength is the word of God.

precepts.why:
“There shall no man be able to stand before you: for the Lord your God shall lay the fear of you and the dread of you upon all the land that ye shall tread upon, as he hath said unto you.”

The nations fear us because God is with us when we are moving right. Look how the other nations look at us in this truth, on the cruises: we are not on the carnival cruise smoking weed and fighting; we sit up in a corner by ourselves, and they all watch us, amazed. Why are they not fighting, not playing rap music, not drinking and drunk? They want to read the shirts. They are not worried about the Christians reading the Bible; they see the spirit of God on us. It is a fear and a dread, because they see we are waking up. We are a phenomenon to them, and it is good to have them on their heels.

They don’t fear you when you are out there arguing about who is better, LeBron or Michael Jordan, Drake or Kendrick Lamar. The Lord lays the fear of you on them when you are moving with him. That is the strength he endued us with.

sense.text: “Of whom we have many things to say, and hard to be uttered, seeing ye are dull of hearing.” Some people are dull of hearing; they can’t understand or perceive.

“For when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again which be the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat.” The milk is the laws, the basics. The strong meat is the prophecies, and exercising your senses so you can discern between right and wrong.

“For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe.” If you are still trying to figure out whether to wear fringes or not eat pork, you are not ready for the deep stuff yet.

“But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.” The reason of use is being exercised in the milk: the deep basics. Understanding the small things, like keeping the commandments, is the foundation of growing in understanding.

Brothers want to bypass that and go into prophecy, and they don’t know how to deal with one another: how to apply Matthew 18 when there is an issue, how to let go of strife and beef, how to endeavour to keep the unity, keep a marriage together and discipline children.

A grown man with gray hair, put fourth in line in a city where a school is being planned, said he didn’t agree that the captain and officers should be over him. He was put out. He did not believe the simple thing, obey them that have rule over you, which is 101. He answers to the white man at his job, so why is he mad? A body can’t grow if men can’t follow structure. He could not discern how his actions would affect his wife, his children and the greater body of Israel. David said he would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of God, and this man is jockeying for position.
“The law shall be found perfect without lies: and wisdom is perfection to a faithful mouth.” This man has the law within his mind.

“A man that hath travelled knoweth many things; and he that hath much experience will declare wisdom.” You have to be travelled in this truth and have experience. Some men have never been out of their own city.

This is speaking of a man that knows God’s laws and travels. Some are in the military and travel, and some are old and have been here and there, but they don’t know anything, because they don’t know the law. Remember the scripture that says days should speak and multitude of years should teach wisdom, but there is a spirit in man. A lot of older brothers lived from the fifties and sixties and amounted to nothing, and they want to be over men, but you have to study first, learn God’s laws and apply them. Age does not put you at that level; spiritually you are still at an infant stage. If you don’t know God’s laws you are an infant, a toddler, according to the word of God, even at eighty years old.

That is why Paul told Timothy, let no man despise thy youth: God chose that man, and he would be over men older than him. It doesn’t make the older man less, but don’t use your age and worldly wisdom to think it will outshine God’s wisdom. God chooses who he wants and where he wants them in his body. Be glad you are part of this mission and play your role.

“He that hath no experience knoweth little: but he that hath travelled is full of prudence. When I travelled, I saw many things; and I understand more than I can express.” When he travelled, the law he already understood let him understand what he saw. He travelled teaching, labouring for the Lord and for our people to wake up, for all them that seek learning.

Military men go to Syria and never see Dura-Europos; they go to Iraq and never see the walls of Cyrus. They travel, but they are not studied to know what to look for. But in travelling while teaching is where you gain experience, and it is part of how you go from milk to meat, because now you can share that experience.

When the brothers first went to Cuba and Captain Abio was teaching, the police came, then a paddy wagon full of cops with nightsticks. Teaching without a licence there carried two years in prison without trial, and the police chief said, based on what you are teaching, we don’t need another revolution. Asked about their rights, he said, You have no rights here. F your rights. Because that was experienced, it is understood there that a different approach is needed. Not that we won’t teach there, but we find another way. That is why it is good to get around learned men who have travelled: there is more than can be expressed in one conversation, and if you stay around and learn, we can tell you, this won’t work here, this is how you approach it.
“I was ofttimes in danger of death: yet I was delivered because of these things.”

“The spirit of those that fear the Lord shall live; for their hope is in him that saveth them. Whoso feareth the Lord shall not fear nor be afraid; for he is his hope.”

You learn that when you travel with certain men. If you are sincere in this truth and really keeping his commandments in your personal life, that spirit jumps on you so that you will not fear. In Trinidad the brothers were told they couldn’t go up into Laventille, that the gangs left only one way down. They went up there and taught, and it put a spirit on those men; now they go up there.

precepts.why: The man that travelled was labouring, and for whom? “Consider that I laboured not for myself only, but for all them that seek learning.” That is the point: you travel the world to teach people that want to learn. But first you have to keep the commandments, learn and study, and then you go out and teach.

“Now therefore, O brethren, let us shew an example to our brethren, because their hearts depend upon us, and the sanctuary, and the house, and the altar, rest upon us.” The people are depending upon us. So it is our job to study, learn and get right, so we can travel and share the word with our people.

Then somebody is going to come behind you, and you will share your experiences with them and teach them. In different countries there are things you can get away with here that you can’t do there, and you won’t know it if you don’t travel and don’t get around leadership to learn.

sense.text: Now to the senses. “The Lord created man of the earth, and turned him into it again. He gave them few days, and a short time, and power also over the things therein. He endued them with strength by themselves, and made them according to his image, And put the fear of man upon all flesh, and gave him dominion over beasts and fowls.”

“They received the use of the five operations of the Lord, and in the sixth place he imparted them understanding, and in the seventh speech, an interpreter of the cogitations thereof.” Cogitation is the act of thinking very carefully and deeply about a subject, a carefully considered thought, meditation: the capacity to think or reflect.

The sixth is understanding and the seventh is speech. Speech is the interpreter of what your mind meditates on; out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.

Thinking and reflecting is one of the senses we have, but it does not work unless it is funneled through the word of God. That is how your mind has to work. If you think on something while you are not moving right, the thought that comes out is going to be off.

“Counsel, and a tongue, and eyes, ears, and a heart, gave he them to understand.” Counsel is one, a tongue another, eyes another, ears another, and a heart another. Not in any order, the seven are counsel, tongue, eyes, ears, heart, understanding and speech.

Counsel is when a man weighs options and determines what should be done, but he must be a godly man and surround himself with godly people. The tongue is the instrument of the body we use to form our words.

The eye is for observation, to examine what is happening. Just by looking you can know a situation isn’t right. Two brothers were working together; one stepped to the back, and when he came back he saw the other hand his phone to a girl and walk away from her. Without hearing anything he knew something was wrong. The brother said it was nothing, then said it was business, then kept repeating himself: a multitude of words. That is your senses being exercised, and why it is good to look at a man’s face when he speaks, because his face tells what is really going on.

A man’s ears hear words, instruction, warning and counsel, and your ears have to be tuned to the subtleties in speech. The heart takes what is seen and heard, processes it and comes to a conclusion; you hear, you see and you process, but to discern between good and evil you have to be spiritual. Understanding is a man comprehending the meaning of a matter and distinguishing between right and wrong. And speech reveals the thoughts that were formed in the heart.

“Withal he filled them with the knowledge of understanding, and shewed them good and evil.” He gave them to understand good and evil. There are many senses the Most High gave us, and a handful of them are touched on in this class.

precepts.why:
“And let the counsel of thine own heart stand: for there is no man more faithful unto thee than it.” But the scripture says in the multitude of counsellors there is safety: as much counsel as you can get helps you make the right decisions. That seems the total opposite. Should we not seek counsel?

The verse before answers it: “But be continually with a godly man, whom thou knowest to keep the commandments of the Lord.” Your everyday life, outside of going out into the world to work, should be spent around godly people. If you are around brothers without understanding, your best bet is to be around people with more understanding than you, so you can level up. How will you know he keeps the commandments? You have to be exercised to discern between good and evil. If you keep the commandments you will be around godly men, because every beast consorteth with his own kind.

“Whose, mind is according to thy mind, and will sorrow with thee, if thou shalt miscarry.” Then your mind is godly; he will sorrow with you and correct you. So when it says let the counsel of your own heart stand, it is because you have sought counsel from a godly man and your mind is guided like his. It is not that you let your own heart’s counsel stand without seeking counsel while you are watching porn and making decisions. Then you will make a mistake. The counsel of your own heart, funneled through the laws of God and the scriptures, lets you make your decisions and stand on them.

“For a man’s mind is sometime wont to tell him more than seven watchmen, that sit above in an high tower.” Seven watchmen are godly men, but your own mind tells you, this is the best move for me.

“And above all this pray to the most High, that he will direct thy way in truth.” Above the counsel of your own heart and above the counsel of a godly man, you go to God and he directs your path. But God does not hear the prayer of sinners.

“Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” So it is not telling you not to get counsel from brothers. Get counsel, balance it with what you think might be right, with a godly mind, and then ask God to direct your path.

Ears have to be tuned to subtleties in speech. “In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise.” Brother, stop talking. You think you are saying something deep, and you are burying yourself. Let your yea be yea and your nay be nay, and everything else is evil.

In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: it does not lack sin. The brother with the phone kept over-explaining. That is what an exercised ear catches.

sense.text:
The eyes. “The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.” The eye here is your mind, the eyes of your understanding.

Single means focused, straight, the only thing you are concentrated on: not double minded, not serving two masters. If your eye is single, you resist your appetites and the lusts you have, you resist the pleasure of sin, and you are on this path. The double-minded man is looking at the Lord and looking at Pornhub, looking at the Lord and in the midst of sin.

“But if thine eye be evil, thy whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is that darkness!”

The brother who handed his phone to the girl: the conversation spiralled into him watching porn, going to the strip club, fornicating, and it got worse. His heart was full of darkness. It wasn’t known at first what it was, only that it was something more, an evil concupiscence. How? From the first thing, him handing that woman his phone with a brother a few feet away, with no fear. Thirty-one years in this, and it is known how this thing goes: if you are bold enough to do that, there is more behind the story. And at 2:30 in the morning the call came.

The world says the eyes are the windows to the soul. There is some validity in it: what you look at draws into your mind, your spirit and your soul. That is why the majority of brothers that watch porn are socially awkward and on their fifth proving stage. In porn the woman is disrespected and there is no conversation, and the brother puts a sister’s head on that body in his mind and doesn’t know how to talk to her anymore.
“No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other.” When your eye is not single, you hate God, because something else has your attention and your draw.

precepts.why: What is the eye that is the light of the body? The mind, as read earlier in Ephesians: “The eyes of your understanding being enlightened; that ye may know what is the hope of his calling, and what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints.” The eye is the understanding.

A single eye is not double minded. “Do ye think that the scripture saith in vain, The spirit that dwelleth in us lusteth to envy? But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble. Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.”

Resist what? If your eye is single, you are resisting all your appetites and the lusts that you have.

“Whoso taketh pleasure in wickedness shall be condemned: but he that resisteth pleasures crowneth his life.” That is the resisting: resisting the pleasure of sin. If your eye is single, you are on that path.
“A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.” The eye that is not single is the double-minded man, looking at the Lord while in the midst of sin.
Remember what Job said about his eyes: “I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?” He wasn’t lusting. His eye was single.

“For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.” You covet what you see; you lust after what you see. That lust of the eyes is not of the Father but of the world.

You are in a spiritual battle and don’t understand what you are fighting. “Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts.” The fleshly lust comes from the things you look at, the lust of the eyes.

“Which war against the soul.” You are at war, brothers, and you are losing. Satan is in your head saying you’ve got this, you have it under control, and next you are giving your number to a girl, with no fear, doing whatever you want. The brother who handed off his phone ended up in a strip club buying sex and going raw; it was no miracle to see it, because he was so far gone.

So when you want to get married, men and women, get blood tests, six months before and again before the wedding, because some diseases lie dormant and pop up. While proving someone, when they get sick with a cold or a sniffle, make them take the test then, because the immune system is weak and whatever is there will show.

sense.text: The eyes and the hearing are physical senses we have. “So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.” In hearing we are able to process what we heard, learn from it and apply it to our lives. Faith increases by hearing the word of God.

precepts.why:
“When all Israel is come to appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose, thou shalt read this law before all Israel in their hearing.” In their hearing.

“Gather the people together, men, and women, and children, and thy stranger that is within thy gates, that they may hear, and that they may learn, and fear the Lord your God, and observe to do all the words of this law: And that their children, which have not known any thing, may hear, and learn to fear the Lord your God.” They hear, and so they learn, fear the Lord and observe to do the law.

So we exercise these senses in what we watch, as in Job 31, and in our hearing, what we take in and listen to. Evil communications corrupt good manners. What you digest through your vision and your hearing will change the way you think. We have to exercise those physical senses so we can tap into the spiritual senses we have, and that is intuition.

sense.text: The tongue, spliced with speech. “Wherefore, Job, I pray thee, hear my speeches, and hearken to all my words. Behold, now I have opened my mouth, my tongue hath spoken in my mouth.”

“My words shall be of the uprightness of my heart: and my lips shall utter knowledge clearly.” Our speech, our tongue, is supposed to be in the edification of God’s words. Exercise those skills in yourself, in listening to the word of God and in speaking it. Let your conversation be seasoned with grace.

“The Spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life. If thou canst answer me, set thy words in order before me, stand up. Behold, I am according to thy wish in God’s stead: I also am formed out of the clay.”

precepts.why:
“The Lord God hath given me the tongue of the learned, that I should know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary.” We have to have a tongue that knows how to speak to the people that are weary. How do we engage them and bring them to repentance, all those that seek learning? It comes from being seasoned and knowing how to work those physical senses to bring out a spiritual message that brings the people to God.

“He wakeneth morning by morning, he wakeneth mine ear to hear as the learned. The Lord God hath opened mine ear, and I was not rebellious, neither turned away back.” When the Lord opened our ear to understand this, we were not to be rebellious and turn away. God decided to show you something and give you an ear to understand it; if at that point you rebel and turn away, you lose that sense of understanding. That is why it says men are dull of hearing. We never turn our back from it.

“Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.” Hear, but don’t understand what is being said; see with your eyes, but don’t perceive what you see.

“Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.” The Lord is saying, I opened your understanding to see and hear, and you rebelled against me. Now go and speak to the people, but I don’t want them to understand, because I want to punish them; I don’t want them to repent yet.

Like men in prison who want to get right: yes, but you still have to do the twenty years. Like a parent: I know you’re sorry, but you’re going to get this ass whooping right now, and you can be sorry after. That is what the Lord says. That is the ear that rebelled and lost its hearing.

“Withal praying also for us, that God would open unto us a door of utterance, to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I am also in bonds: That I may make it manifest, as I ought to speak. Walk in wisdom toward them that are without, redeeming the time. Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man.”

Let your tongue and your speech be seasoned with grace. How do you get that? Get around men of understanding, learn, repent, and exercise those senses. When you do that, you will discern what to say.

“Wisdom raineth down skill and knowledge of understanding standing, and exalteth them to honour that hold her fast.” Having that skill: the voice, the tongue seasoned to know how to speak and how to engage.

Brothers have people right in front of them listening and paying attention, and stop speaking to them to go deal with a heckler. Learn how to fish the people in and keep them engaged. A lot of brothers talk at the people, not to them. Say the things that are going to trigger them: you’re tired of working for a little bit of money; would you like to be where you never have to work again, never get sick, with your family all there? Then this is what you have to do to get that. Lead them in. You learn that by getting around seasoned men and exercising those skills.

“Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things.” The tongue is small in your mouth, but it can boast great things. “Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth!” The tongue can spark a fire and cause much trouble by the things you say.

“And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity.” The tongue has gotten people kicked out of their homes and caused divorce; it causes all devastations. Sirach says the same, how a tongue has cast out virtuous women. Susanna almost lost her life because of a lie.

sense.text:
The heart, spliced with understanding. “Then opened I my mouth, and, behold, he reached me a full cup, which was full as it were with water, but the colour of it was like fire. And I took it, and drank: and when I had drunk of it, my heart uttered understanding, and wisdom grew in my breast, for my spirit strengthened my memory.”

The cup is wisdom taken in: we take it in, we drink it. And the spirit strengthened his memory. That happens by taking in the word, by repetition, reading over and over. You can never read the scriptures enough. The minute you think you know something you are deceiving yourself; there is another layer you have not touched.

That is why it is imperative to get around people of understanding and learn. Even leadership still hears precepts never heard before and asks, what was that precept? You strengthen your memory by being consistent, and this has to be your chief joy. Then you are exercising the sense of understanding: when people speak, you remember the scriptures and know, no, that is not what that means, or yes, that is correct.

precepts.why: Of Aaron: “He gave unto him his commandments, and authority in the statutes of judgments, that he should teach Jacob the testimonies, and inform Israel in his laws.” The memory is strengthened so that you can go and teach the people.

“God give you wisdom in your heart to judge his people in righteousness.” Rightly dividing the word of truth, discerning between right and wrong. The heart is supposed to take in, learn, memorize and strengthen the memory, so you can judge his people in righteousness.

“That their good things be not abolished, and that their glory may endure for ever.” Our job is to lead people to God, so that the good things they learned are not abolished. You remind them: stay faithful; if you are going through something, this is what the scripture says.

Many times men and women have a way out of their situations and don’t take it, and when it blows up in their face they wonder why. It is because the recall of scripture isn’t there; they haven’t opened the book, so they don’t know where to go or how to fight. What scripture do you go to for lust, or for depression? You have to drink the word, and it strengthens your memory to give you recall.

sense.text:
Counsel is when a man weighs options and determines what should be done. “As timber girt and bound together in a building cannot be loosed with shaking: so the heart that is stablished by advised counsel shall fear at no time.”

Always bounce what you think off of men of understanding, and ask questions. Most of the time, when a person does not ask for counsel, it is because they don’t want to be told that what they are doing is wrong, and most of the time they already know it is wrong.

In his early years in the truth, Bishop Kani told the Bishop he wanted to move to Florida and was told to sit down, that he didn’t know anything. He reasoned with himself: is the Bishop trying to teach me to sin against God? No. Why go to Florida? Because his mother would put down money on a house. So he stayed. Ten years later he asked again and was told to go and build. Had he not listened the first time, he would not be in the truth today. Back then he also brought leadership a precept he thought would let them smoke weed, on mandrakes, and the Bishop laughed, said, Nigga, shut up, and kicked him out of the office. Had he left with that understanding, he would be a weed head today. Thank the Lord.

precepts.why:
The greatest gift a young man can have is the art of listening; it will save you so much headache. Leadership has no skin in the game to lead you wrong and can save you from major mistakes, because they have experienced them or seen them happen. You can cut the curve, or do it your way and see how it works out.

“Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.” Listen to counsel in your young days so you can be wise in the latter part of your life. Do it while you are young and can figure it out. Sometimes just be quiet, because what comes out of your mouth while you are unlearned is going to be nonsense. Listen, preserve yourself, and in that you strengthen your senses to discern.

“There are many devices in a man’s heart; nevertheless the counsel of the Lord, that shall stand.” We have all kinds of devices in our hearts, bright ideas that are not right, but the counsel of the Lord is what shall stand.

sense.text:
From the physical senses to the spiritual senses that you exercise going from milk to meat. Clairvoyance is the ability to gain information about past, present or future events beyond the natural senses, described as clear seeing in the mind’s eye. This mind has an eye; you can foresee certain things. Another way of saying it is prophetic vision: seeing things other people can’t see.

“If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make myself known unto him in a vision, and will speak unto him in a dream.” If there is a prophet among you, God will give him a vision and show him things people can’t see.

We are living through one right now. The Lord used the Bishop to put us in purple, back when everybody wore hodgepodge colours and looked like Babylon. There was pushback, sisters and some effeminate brothers arguing against it, and other camps clowned us, not understanding that it is biblical and that our Lord and Saviour was dressed like that. It was a deliberate, conscious decision to uniform us and separate us from all the other groups, many of them lunatics, because what we teach is drastically different. Now others are trying to wear purple. It was a prophetic vision of something that was going to happen, put upon him to see.

These are the spiritual senses being activated. “And Elisha prayed, and said, Lord, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And the Lord opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.”

The Lord showed him something no one else could see. In the spiritual realm there are angels all around us; the Lord said where two or three are gathered, I am in the midst. We don’t see that, but the Lord will open up the spirit and make it evident. A time will come when some of us will see things, and God will whisper in our ears, show us, direct our path and reveal things to us that the world cannot see.

But you have to move from milk to meat to tap into that. If you are still caught up in your old sins you won’t be able to see these things or have foresight.

Clairaudience is hearing sounds and voices beyond normal physical hearing. Many have experienced something in their spirit telling and guiding them: don’t go down that street, you’ll get locked up; leave that woman alone, she will be the death of you.

“That the Lord called Samuel: and he answered, Here am I. And he ran unto Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou calledst me.” Samuel thought Eli was calling him. “Now Samuel did not yet know the Lord, neither was the word of the Lord yet revealed unto him.” Those that read four chapters a day would know this history.
“And Eli perceived that the Lord had called the child.” Eli perceived that the Lord was calling him. That is clairaudience, a spiritual level of a sixth sense.

“Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth.” Samuel finally said, Lord, I am here, I hear you. That was an inner hearing, a spiritual hearing: no voice uttering, but he heard it within. That is his conscience.

precepts.why:
Elijah said, “I have been very jealous for the Lord God of hosts: for the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away.” They were out to kill him.

“The Lord was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the Lord was not in the earthquake: And after the earthquake a fire; but the Lord was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.” That still small voice was the Lord speaking to him.

“And it was so, when Elijah heard it, that he wrapped his face in his mantle.” The Lord was not in the wind, the earthquake or the fire, but a small voice uttered to Elijah and communicated with him that only he could hear. That again is a sense, a spiritual sixth sense, where the Lord deals with a man.

“In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falleth on men, Fear came upon me, and trembling, which made all my bones to shake. Then a spirit passed before my face; the hair of my flesh stood up.” A spirit passed before him. He sensed an aura around him; he could not see it, but he knew it was there.

“It stood still, but I could not discern the form thereof: an image was before mine eyes.” His spiritual eyes saw an image, and he felt it. “There was silence, and I heard a voice.” There was silence, yet he heard a voice. That speech was happening in his spirit.

“Shall mortal man be more just than God? shall a man be more pure than his maker?” That is the inner voice, clairaudience, God’s voice speaking to him. Some of us have experienced it: the Lord telling you not to do something, or to do something. If you are spiritual and sincerely keeping his commandments, you had better listen to it; that is the spiritual sense trying to guide you and direct your path, and it will not lead you to do anything evil. But if you are not spiritual, and are in the midst of sin doing evil, that could be Satan guiding you and telling you to do wrong.

sense.text:
Clairsentience means clear feeling, sensing things intuitively. Another word for it is discerning of spirits: an intuition that tells you something, a spirit of discernment on people.

“To another faith by the same Spirit; to another the gifts of healing by the same Spirit; To another the working of miracles; to another prophecy; to another discerning of spirits.” These are gifts God gives to men. With the discernment of spirits you read people; you can read a person’s spirit.

precepts.why: “To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.” If they are not speaking according to the law and the testimony of the scriptures, God is not dealing with that. That is discerning between good and evil, and it behooves you to study, so that when people speak you know whether what they say is right or wrong.

“Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.” They might appear right and sound good, but because you study, you can rightly divide what they say. Somebody could be the devil and speak softly, cry and tug on your heartstrings, but if you are spiritual and know the word of God, you discern that he is coming with all manner of guile and deceit.

“For such are false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ.” These men transform themselves into the apostles of Christ. “And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.” Knowing that, you need a spirit of discernment.

“Therefore it is no great thing if his ministers also be transformed as the ministers of righteousness; whose end shall be according to their works.” You have to discern between these men; they are false apostles teaching lies. Other groups teach that we are the Israelites and call themselves the home of the truth, but they have a barbecue on the sabbath day. They look the part, but you discern that they are not of that sort.

“Beloved, believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God: because many false prophets are gone out into the world.” Because many false prophets are gone out into the world, you need a discerning spirit. That is clairsentience, the discerning of spirits.

sense.text:
Claircognizance is clear knowing: suddenly understanding something or getting an answer without being told. There are things you know clearly that you don’t need anybody to explain to you, a sudden knowledge, if you are spiritual.

“But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession, And kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it.” A couple sold property and kept back part of the price, and it was their property anyway. They didn’t have to lie.

“But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land?” Nobody had to tell Peter that. He already knew. That was the spirit of God working those senses: when he saw him, he knew something wasn’t right with this man’s spirit, that he was dealing evil right then. A spiritual man discerneth all things.
“Whiles it remained, was it not thine own? and after it was sold, was it not in thine own power? why hast thou conceived this thing in thine heart? thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God.”

“And Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost: and great fear came on all them that heard these things.” The great fear was that Peter was able to discern lies from truth. How did he know?

Many have been in a moment of not moving right when the Bishop says, you in the spirit, brother? And the brother thinks, how does he know? Faces crack, heads go down like they are reading the script. We laugh because we know it is true.

precepts.why:
“As the palate tasteth divers kinds of venison: so doth an heart of understanding false speeches.” When you eat, you don’t have to see the food to tell chicken from beef, or beef from fish. So when a person has false speech, a heart of understanding discerns it.

One way: in the multitude of words there wanteth not sin. You are talking too much. You don’t have to convince anyone of the truth; let your yea be yea and your nay be nay. When a man starts with, let me explain, there it is.

sense.text: This is sudden knowing. “Then Daniel went in, and desired of the king that he would give him time, and that he would shew the king the interpretation.” The king’s wise men could not tell the dream and its interpretation, because the king would not tell them the dream; the king did not remember it himself. So they asked Daniel, and Daniel asked for time to give the understanding.

“Then Daniel went to his house, and made the thing known to Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions: That they would desire mercies of the God of heaven concerning this secret; that Daniel and his fellows should not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.”

“Then was the secret revealed unto Daniel in a night vision.” God said in Numbers 12 he would make himself known in a vision and speak in a dream. Suddenly Daniel understood what the whole thing was about, because God imparted it upon him.

“Blessed be the name of God for ever and ever: for wisdom and might are his: And he changeth the times and the seasons: he removeth kings, and setteth up kings: he giveth wisdom unto the wise, and knowledge to them that know understanding.”

He gives knowledge to them that know understanding. You have to know understanding before God will reveal certain things to you. That is going from milk to meat: you can’t expect it without first gaining a certain level of understanding. Meat is for those of full age.

“He revealeth the deep and secret things: he knoweth what is in the darkness, and the light dwelleth with him.” “For thou hast now made known unto us the king’s matter.”

The king’s matter was something the king himself didn’t remember, but by that clear knowing God made it plain to Daniel all at once. This is the level of activating the spiritual senses, and it begins with application. We all have it on some level when we move right with God.

“While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.”

We have to have foresight and understand that the things we don’t see in front of us are the prophecies that are going to come to pass: the understanding of what will happen at the end, which the Lord is revealing to us.

precepts.why:
“Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.” The evidence of things not seen: things buried in the scriptures that God reveals to his servants the prophets. He makes clear to us the things necessary for salvation and reveals spiritual things that the world will never be able to see.

But first you have to move from milk to meat.
